paragraphs: Here's what Job teaches me, friend: a faithful life isn't one clean room. It's the whole house. Job says, “I have made a covenant with my eyes” (Job 31:1), and then he keeps going through his money, his servants, the poor, his enemies and even his own hidden guilt. I spent years in a junk drawer, so I know it's easy to keep the front room spotless and shove everything else to the back. Job is walking through every drawer in the house and saying, "Check them ALL."

Why would a man do that? Because he says, “Does He not see my ways and count my every step?” (Job 31:4). If God sees every step, then the heart, the hands and the open door all matter, not just what the neighbors can see. That's why Job asks God to “weigh me with honest scales” (Job 31:6). Friend, most of us want a little grace on the scale, and this man is asking for an HONEST one.

Now hear the end of his speech, because it matters. Job doesn't want to hide and he doesn't want to go quiet. He says, “Let the Almighty answer me” (Job 31:35). So here's your question, baker: if God opened up your whole day, would the person in the dark match the person in the light? Job has finished speaking, but this story is NOT over.
